summary: Idaho Peak lookout above New Denver, listed on BC's community heritage register; trail public, lookout locked, and no staffing or fire record found.

facts.design: Square building with a concrete block foundation and a flat roof

access.note: Firelookout.ca says the trail is public and the lookout is locked.

visit.trail_note: Ridge walk through summer wildflowers to the lookout, 7.2 km per the Wakefield Trail guide. A 10Adventures notice says a mudslide washed out the trailhead road; the notice is undated.

events.note: Register gives 1940 as the build date for the Idaho Peak Recreation Site entry, which describes the fire lookout.
Listed on the Community Heritage Register (Canadian Register of Historic Places entry 22697), recognized by local governments under the Local Government Act, s.954.

evidence.supports: Register describes the lookout as a good example of 1940s-60s fire lookouts, with a concrete block foundation, square massing and a flat roof
evidence.quote: The Idaho Peak Lookout is a good representation of the fire lookouts of the 1940s-60s, with a concrete block foundation, square massing, and a flat roof

evidence.supports: Register gives 1940 as the build date
Site is southeast of New Denver in the Selkirk Mountains
evidence.quote: located southeast of New Denver in the Selkirk Mountain Range in BC

evidence.supports: Lookout is at the summit and connected to the BC Forest Service; the 2020 entry describes it as present
evidence.quote: an important connection to the British Columbia Forest Service in the fire lookout present at the apex of Idaho Peak

evidence.supports: Fire lookouts of the period were stationed at these sites during summer months
evidence.quote: fire lookouts who were stationed at these sites during the summer months

evidence.supports: Residents and visitors come each summer
evidence.quote: Local residents and tourists alike flock to this place each summer

evidence.supports: Recognized by local governments in BC under the Local Government Act, April 2020
Current function of the site is park

notes_for_editor: Brief access 'unknown' is now 'restricted' from Firelookout.ca's 'Trail is public, lookout is locked.' Firelookout.ca shows Year Built and Structure Height as N/A, so its page gives no build year. The 1940 build date comes from the register entry for the recreation site, which describes the fire lookout as its historic function; the story says so. historicplaces.ca returned only its page title, so register facts come from the Heritage Guide copy of entry 22697. No staffing, fire or named-keeper source was found in two searches; those topics are left out. The 10Adventures road notice is undated and may be stale. Facebook (Lost Kootenays) and sitesandtrailsbc REC2128 returned no readable text.
